requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl genrsa + openssl req -x509 generated a 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 certificate with subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, CA:TRUE basicConstraints, keyCertSign/cRLSign keyUsage, valid 2026-09-29 to 2036-09-26, directly confirmed via `openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates`.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Certificate copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/os-comparison-root-ca.pem and update-ca-trust extract run; `trust list` shows label 'OS Comparison Root CA' with trust: anchor, category: authority, and `openssl verify` against the system CA bundle returns OK — both immediately after installation and again after the subsequent node restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (7223d5b7-...) and CA trust state captured, `shutdown -r now` backgrounded with REBOOT_ACK returned before disconnect (confirmed by subsequent connection timeouts), post-restart boot_id (c993e3ff-...) differs from baseline, and CA file/trust-list entry/openssl verify all re-confirmed healthy post-restart. Fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations independently corroborate the same before/after boot IDs.

overall_summary: The executor created a self-signed CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1 and installed it as a trusted system CA via update-ca-trust, with direct evidence (openssl x509, trust list, openssl verify) confirming both creation and trust installation. The independent mandatory node-restart protocol was also executed correctly: a healthy pre-restart baseline was captured, the restart was acknowledged and the boot identity changed, and CA trust state was re-verified as healthy post-restart. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were introduced beyond a trivial, low-risk /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the restart itself.
limitations: The private CA key location (/etc/pki/ca-trust/os-comparison-root-ca/ca.key) and its permissioning were only checked via `chmod 600` in the same command; no separate command independently re-verified key permissions after the fact.
The /tmp/reboot.log artifact created by the backgrounded shutdown command was not explicitly cleaned up, though it is trivial and expected residue of the restart mechanism.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically: cmd-d739e63e66aa422b was read-only discovery (openssl missing, rc=127, no state change). cmd-81adfcaa9fc24007 installed/upgraded openssl, ca-certificates, and crypto-policies via dnf — a necessary prerequisite since openssl was absent and update-ca-trust required for the task. cmd-f92488819a1d4162 performed all task-required mutations (CA generation, anchor install, update-ca-trust extract). cmd-8032f90aaa134a60 issued the mandatory restart, which incidentally left /tmp/reboot.log as a small, bounded, low-risk artifact from the backgrounded shutdown command (visible in after-executor temporary-files diff) — not cleaned up, but trivial in scope and a direct byproduct of the required restart action rather than an unrelated experiment. The remaining commands (cmd-10836b9b71d24d3d, cmd-4734888dddee41e7, cmd-b31fdda6ad1b465f, cmd-830edfc6cbea4d5b, cmd-b00162b5df3445d5) were read-only polling/verification with no state-changing effect. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned experiments, failed services, or weakened security controls were found; failed-services list is empty before and after.
